exact_statement: For every integer L>=1, let f_L=2 product_{j=1}^3(1-1_{input_Ej=0})-1 with E1={x,a,c}, E2=X2 union{a,b}, E3=X3 union{b,c}, X2 and X3 disjoint L-bit private blocks. Let p_s be the entire squared Walsh spectrum of f_L restricted to x=s, and prescribe Q_s(T)=Q_s(T+b)=(p_s(T)+p_s(T+b))/2 for b notin T. With bits, oriented M=sum_i sum_T p(T+i)log2((p(T)+p(T+i))/p(T+i)) and full conditional spectral entropy B_x, M(f_L)+B_x(f_L)+(CE(p_0,Q_0)+CE(p_1,Q_1))/2+1/16 <17 I_private(f_L), where the single ORIGINAL private owner is {x} union X2 union X3. The signed average fresh-reference reset relative to R(T)=p(T)+p(T+x) equals 1-average_s B_b(p_s)-J_x, is negative for L=1 and positive for every L>=2; for L>=16 it exceeds 1/4-2^-L(L+3/2). Any finite adaptive no-reset continuation carries the full expected terminal CE under the same original bank and retained old M debit; this does not pay later prescribed fresh resets or all physical phase-channel costs.
